players.product: retail colocation & interconnection (IBX data centers, Equinix Fabric) and xScale hyperscale data centers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Adaire Fox-Martin framed enterprise AI demand as four distinct deployment use cases that are all scaling simultaneously inside Equinix data centers: 'stack' (the customer's own stack placed in an Equinix facility to run open models on private AI infrastructure and reduce token cost), 'sovereign' (data residency and compliance, supported by geo-fencing software), 'batch' (AI factories for training and batch inferencing, enabled by liquid cooling) and latency-sensitive agentic workloads that must sit in-metro (which also cuts backhaul cost). She said 'We have 60% of the Fortune 500 sitting at Equinix' and that the company is 'operating in 36 countries today', so it is 'sovereign almost by design'.
quarterly_data.figure: 60% of the Fortune 500; operating in 36 countries; four use cases (stack, sovereign, batch, latency sensitive)

quarterly_data.signal: New software layer for the interconnection business: Fox-Martin described 'Equinix Fabric Intelligence' inside the Equinix environment, which 'allows you to adjust, to heal a network in real time, to have agents manage autonomously the creation of paths across that network in real time'. Positioning: most customer networks today 'are built for performance, they're not built for compliance' - with Equinix you get both, including staying inside a jurisdiction.

Power and community strategy: Fox-Martin said Equinix has 'always adopted the principle that we fund any energy or grid infrastructure costs directly ourselves that are driven by the requirement to drive the workloads in our data centers, not passing those on to domestic ratepayers', citing several such closings across the year with 'the most recent one just in Hampton'. She also pointed to the company's 'investments in SMR technology and bring our own in adding to the grid' as part of how it sources and innovates for energy.
